explanation: Carry the binary value of the root-to-current path. Append each node bit by shifting left and adding it; a leaf contributes that completed value, while an internal node contributes the sum from its children.
timeComplexity: O(n) time. Each node adds its bit to one prefix; only the active root-to-node recursion path is retained.
spaceComplexity: O(h) recursion space for tree height h. Each active recursive frame holds one path prefix; paths are not materialized.
attribution: Unmodified EPIJudge reference source: epi_judge_java_solutions/epi/SumRootToLeaf.java. Original contributors; repository LICENSE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/).
correctness: On entry to a node, prefix is the binary number represented by its ancestors. Shifting left and adding the node’s bit therefore gives the value of the path ending there. A leaf contributes exactly one completed root-to-leaf number. Internal nodes partition all remaining paths into their left and right subtrees, so summing those recursive contributions counts every path once.
walkthrough: For tree [1, 0, 1, 1, null, 0, 1], the three root-to-leaf bit paths are 101, 110 and 111. Their decimal values are 5, 6 and 7. The left subtree contributes 5 and the right subtree contributes 13, giving total 18. The walkthroughCase uses the judge’s JSON input format and expected observation.
edgeCases: Leading zero bits still consume a path position but do not increase its numeric value.
Each leaf contributes separately, even when two different paths encode the same number.
